rows.answer: Eligibility for the PM-KISAN scheme is primarily based on landholding, with the definition of a landholder farmer’s family as "a family comprising of husband, wife, and minor children who own cultivable land as per land records of the concerned State/UT" [pmkisan:operational_guidelines_2019:0001]. However, certain categories are excluded, including institutional land holders, and farmer families where one or more members belong to specific high-income or professional categories such as former and present holders of constitutional posts, former and present Ministers, and serving or retired government employees with a monthly pension of Rs.10,000 or more, among others [pmkisan:operational_guidelines_2019:0002].

rows.answer: No, a serving or retired officer and employee of the Central/State Government Ministries/Offices/Departments and its field units, Central or State Public Sector Enterprises (PSEs) and Attached offices/Autonomous Institutions under Government, as well as regular employees of local bodies, are not eligible to get benefit under the PM-KISAN scheme [chunk_id: pmkisan:faq:0003]. However, serving or retired Multi Tasking Staff/Class IV/Group D employees are eligible if their families meet the other criteria and are not covered under other exclusion criteria.

rows.answer: Yes, land transferred between December 2018 and January 2019 is eligible for PM-KISAN benefits. According to the operational guidelines [pmkisan:operational_guidelines_2019:0003], in cases where the transfer of ownership of cultivable land has happened between December 1, 2018, and January 31, 2019, due to reasons such as purchase, succession, will, or gift, the first installment during the financial year (2018-19) shall be a proportionate amount from the date of transfer till March 31, 2019, with respect to the 4 months period.

rows.answer: Eligibility for a PMAY-G house is based on housing deprivation parameters from the Socio-Economic and Caste Census (SECC) 2011 data, specifically targeting households that are houseless or living in zero, one, or two rooms with kutcha walls and roofs [chunk_id: pmayg:framework_for_implementation_2022:0007]. Additional beneficiaries may be identified from the Awaas+ list [chunk_id: pmayg:framework_for_implementation_2022:0007]. Households must also meet other criteria, such as not having availed benefits from other government schemes or constructed a pucca house from their own funds [chunk_id: pmayg:framework_for_implementation_2022:0027].

rows.answer: Yes, a family living in a kutcha house may qualify for PMAY-G. According to the framework for implementation of PMAY-G [pmayg:framework_for_implementation_2022:0007], the scheme aims to provide pucca houses with basic amenities to households living in kutcha and dilapidated houses in rural areas. The selection of beneficiaries is based on housing deprivation parameters from the Socio Economic and Caste Census (SECC), 2011 data, which includes households living in kutcha houses.
